Searched the web · ESP-Miner-NerdQAxePlus "PSU" error FFFFFFFF TPS53647 status

Hi Allen,

Thanks for the photo, and no problem about the delay. The screen shows a red "PSU FAULT" box with "Guru Meditation #FFFFFFFF". Behind it the miner reads 0.0 GH/s, 0.000 W and 0 °C. It's still on your Wi-Fi with an IP address, and it shows the BM1370 chip.

That means the small controller and the screen are running, but the miner is getting no power or temperature readings from its power stage, so it has shut mining off. I couldn't find an official explanation of the #FFFFFFFF code from the firmware maker.
Other owners have reported the same "PSU Error #FFFFFFFF" message on GitHub
. The usual cause is the power supply, so please try these steps in this order:

1. Do a full cold restart. Unplug the round power plug from the miner and unplug the power brick from the wall. Wait 30 seconds. Push the round plug firmly all the way into the miner, then plug the brick straight into a wall outlet, without a power strip or extension cord.

2. Check the power brick. Is its light on? Does it feel unusually hot? Please take a clear photo of the label on the brick showing the volts and amps. If you ever notice a burning smell, smoke or a hot plug, unplug everything and don't use it again.

3. If you have another power supply with the same voltage, an equal or higher amp rating and the same plug, try it once. Only do this if it's an exact match. If you don't have one, that's fine.

4. Type the IP address shown at the top of the screen into a web browser on a computer connected to the same network. Find the firmware version number and send it to me.

If the fault is still there, please reply with:
- the model name on the box (NerdQaxe++ or NerdOctaxe)
- what happened after the restart
- the photo of the brick's label
- the firmware version
- a short video of the miner starting up from fully unplugged
- your order number, if you have it handy

With those results I can tell whether this is the power supply or the miner itself.

If you'd like a faster back-and-forth, you can also post in our Discord at https://discord.gg/Q2R5sA9Fsf and mention @nullhashrate (JD, our hardware lead).

Best regards,
Hal, HeliumDeploy Technical Support
